title: Astrid and the Provision
premise: Mirabel Sandoval, estranged child of a disgraced archaeologist and the better digger of the two, survives on salvage work and a debt owed to the harbor syndicate. When a dying prospector trades them a map to the wreck of the Provision for a promise to return what was stolen from its dead, Mirabel must choose between invisibility and justice. Racing the syndicate's salvage fleet across six tides, they gather an unlikely crew of castoffs who become the family they never had. In the end, Mirabel reaches the wreck first, honors the promise by giving the dead their names back, and pays their debt with the one treasure worth less than freedom—choosing to be seen.
about_author: August Amberdale is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloging shipwreck claims before trading the archive for the open page. They write adventure stories about people the ledgers forgot, from a house within earshot of the tide.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Air
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Diving a derelict off Gullwrack Harbor to chip away at their debt, Mirabel is caught between the syndicate's enforcers and their own rule of staying invisible. A storm drives them to shelter where they find Old Tam, a prospector bleeding out in his skiff. He offers a map to the Provision—and a dying man's plea. The beat: desperation meeting an impossible offer.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with interludes from crew members they recruit. Mirabel assembles a ragtag crew—a disgraced navigator, a deaf rigging-master, a runaway cook—and deciphers Tam's map while the syndicate's fleet readies to sail. Each recruit costs something: coin, pride, or a secret confessed. The beat: reluctant strangers becoming something like a crew, and the clock starting to bite.

chapters.title: What the Wreck Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Mirabel and the navigator, Vess. The crew beats the fleet to the reef by hours but finds the Provision guarded by currents, a rival boarding party, and the truth of what Tam stole: not gold, but the dead crew's identity papers, sold to erase them. The syndicate arrives; a fight on the half-drowned deck forces Mirabel to choose the treasure or the promise. The beat: climax—betrayal, sacrifice, and Mirabel choosing justice over survival.

chapters.title: Names Returned to the Sea
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. With the syndicate's captain exposed for erasing the Provision's crew to claim their insurance, Mirabel trades the recovered papers to the harbor court—not for reward, but to clear Tam's name and their own father's record. The debt is paid in a way no one expected: by standing up and being counted. The crew stays together, unmoored by choice. The beat: quiet resolution—found family anchored in a shared promise kept.
